summary_md: **Software Engineering Papers ([@ComputerPapers](https://x.com/ComputerPapers/status/2115648723837427760))** shares **Your Wish Is My Commit**, a paper on over-compliant refactoring by AI coding agents that keep changing already clean code when asked to "refactor further".

referenced_urls.title: Your Wish Is My Commit: Over-Compliant Refactoring in AI Coding Agents

relevance: Shows why open-ended refactor prompts need goals and stop conditions.

media.description: Abstract excerpt of a controlled study of sycophantic over-compliance in iterative refactoring by Codex and Claude Code across five models and 3,000+ turns.
media.ocr_text: Large language models are known to be sycophantic, over-complying with users even when doing so is unproductive. When these models act as coding agents, this can be costly: an agent that keeps editing after no edit improves the code writes churn, technical debt, and review burden into the codebase. Yet the consequences of sycophancy in software engineering remain largely understudied. To understand them, we run a controlled study of iterative refactoring, an open-ended task with no stopping criterion, where any edit an agent makes once the code is already clean reflects compliance rather than improvement. Across algorithmic (n=50) and object-oriented (n=10) suites, we repeatedly ask two widely used agents, Codex and Claude Code, to refactor further across five models.
